# cc-switch bridge
中文说明

Every Anthropic-compatible provider saved in the local
cc-switch app becomes one provider route in D

eepSeek
Harness, so its models appear in the model picker and switch like built-in models.
## What it reads

`~/.cc-switch/cc-switch.db` (read-only), table `providers`, rows with `app_type` `claude` /
`claude-

desktop`. From each row: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
the mod

el ids from `meta.stackModels` and the `ANTHROPIC_*MODEL` env keys (`model[1M]` labels keep the
id a

nd give the context window), plus the row name as the group title. Rows are re-read every 60s and
on
every model-picker open, so edits made in cc-switch show up without restarting Harness.
Rows whose `meta.apiFormat` is anything but `anthropic`, or without a base URL / credential / model,

are skipped and logged. Codex rows are imported through the built-in pi-ai adapter instead (see
Set
tings page); the other tool groups store their own shapes, see "Why some groups are not imported".
## What it registers
One `ctx.llm.registerAdapter()` route per provider (`ccswitch-<first 8 chars of the cc-switch id>`),

speaking Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`, SSE or plain JSON) and translating the reply into
Harn

ess stream chunks: text, reasoning/thinking, tool calls, usage, finish reasons. Tool
call/result pai

ring is repaired before sending, because one unanswered tool call makes the upstream
reject the whol

paired before sending, because one unanswered tool call makes the upstream
reject the whole session.
## Thinking levels

The levels are not the bridge's own ladder: cc-switch already declares them per model, and the
Harne
ss menu mirrors that declaration, so both apps offer the same choices.

- `codex` rows carry `modelCatalog.models[].reasoningLevels` (+ `defaultReasoningLevel`), which is
w

hat cc-switch shows for a Codex provider.
- `pi` rows carry `thinkingLevelMap`, where a `null` value

means the level is not offered.
- The row with the same provider name wins; the same model id under

another provider only fills in
what that row does not say.
`none` in cc-switch is `off` here. Hosts whose endpoint cannot replay a thinking block are excluded

in
`replaysWithoutThinking()` in `lib/thinking.js`, and the plugin config `thinking: false` drops ev

utThinking()` in `lib/thinking.js`, and the plugin config `thinking: false` drops every
effort menu.
## Settings page

Settings → **cc-switch-bridge** lists the tool groups your cc-switch actually has configured
(Claude

Code, Claude Code Desktop, Codex, …) and imports the ones you tick. Changing the selection
re-syncs
immediately — no restart — and the model picker follows.
| Group                                                          | How it is imported
| Claude Code / Claude Code Desktop / any Anthropic-format group | the bridge's own adapter, one rou
te per provider

|
| Codex
| handed to the built-in `dsh-llm-pi-ai` adapter
: one provider per cc-switch Codex row, `api` taken from the row's `wire_api` (`openai-responses` /

`openai-completions`), base URL and model catalog straight from the row |
| pi / openclaw / opencode
| each stores its own app's config structure and the bridge h
as no parser for it yet, so they are listed as not importable

|
| gemini
| this machine's row is an empty config, so there is nothing to import
The Codex handoff needs no manual setup: turning it on writes a `codex` entry into the `dsh-llm-pi-a

i`
plugin config in the desktop profile patch (`settingsNs: codex`) and stores each row's key in the
credential store under `CCSWITCH_CODEX_<row>`. Turning it off again removes both the routes and the
secrets the bridge wrote.

### Why some groups are not imported
Not a model problem and not a protocol problem: cc-switch stores one config structure per tool, and

the
bridge only parses two of them — `claude` / `claude-desktop` (`env.ANTHROPIC_*`) and `codex` (TO
bridge only parses two of them — `claude` / `claude-desktop` (`env.ANTHROPIC_*`) and `codex` (TOML).
| Group      | What cc-switch actually stores                                                      |
Status                                             |
| `pi`       | `baseUrl` / `api` / `models[]` / `thinkingLevelMap` — pi-ai's own provider shape    |

fields map almost 1:1, not implemented yet         |
| `openclaw` | `baseUrl` / `api` / `models[]`,
also pi-ai-shaped                                   | not implemented yet

|
| `opencode` | AI SDK `{npm, options, models}` (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` / `@ai-sdk/anthr

opic`) | needs a small `npm → api` map, not implemented yet |
| `gemini`   | `{"env":{},"config":{}}
` (empty on this machine)                                    | nothing to import
s machine)                                    | nothing to import                                  |
The first three would ride the same pi-ai handoff once parsed; no Harness change needed.
## Status file
`~/.dsh/dsh-cc-switch-bridge.status.json` — written after each successful sync: which routes and mod

els
the host process actually holds. First place to look when a provider is missing from the picker.
## Ordering

The bridged and pi-ai rows can be dragged to reorder them; the saved order (`order` in the state
